subject.title: Add opt-in Tailscale Serve with tailnet identity authentication for generated WSL gateways

question: Should generated WSL gateways opt in to trusting Tailscale identity and tailnet ACLs as an additional gateway authorization path managed by Companion?
rationale: The repository cannot infer whether core setup should install and operate Tailscale or treat tailnet identity as authorization; that choice changes the gateway trust boundary and long-term recovery obligations.

options.title: Approve the guarded opt-in
options.body: Allow the feature only when explicitly enabled, retain token and device authentication, forbid Funnel, validate matching MagicDNS tailnets before replacement, and require complete secret redaction and recovery proof.

options.title: Provision Serve without identity trust
options.body: Permit managed private WSS publication but continue requiring normal OpenClaw token or device credentials for every gateway connection.

options.title: Keep Tailscale user-managed
options.body: Continue supporting manually configured .ts.net endpoints while leaving Tailscale installation, Serve lifecycle, and identity policy outside Companion setup.

recommendation.title: Approve the guarded opt-in
recommendation.body: Allow the feature only when explicitly enabled, retain token and device authentication, forbid Funnel, validate matching MagicDNS tailnets before replacement, and require complete secret redaction and recovery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They reopened the issue after cleanup, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the unresolved trust-boundary decision.
